subject: body
title: Meals and Snacks
about: Three meals with snacks in between, a snack with two food groups, the balanced plate (half fruits and vegetables, a quarter grains, a quarter protein, dairy on the side), spotting what a plate is missing, a three-group breakfast, eating together, the serving spoon for shared bowls, sitting while eating, eating slowly, thanking the cook, and kid-sized kitchen jobs. NC 1.NPA.1.2 (foods and why we eat them), 1.PCH.1.2 (keeping germs out of shared food) and 1.PCH.2.1 (spotting what can cause injury, like running with food). Read it together and let him be the plate checker at dinner.
tip: Hand him the job of plate checker: is half the plate fruits and veggies? What is missing?

cards.q: How many meals do most kids eat each day?
cards.note: Breakfast, lunch and dinner, plus one or two small snacks in between.

cards.q: Breakfast, lunch and dinner are the meals. What small bites come in between?
cards.note: A snack in the afternoon, maybe one in the morning. Snacks are little bites that keep you going until the next meal.

cards.q: A good snack is like a tiny meal. Which snack has two food groups?
cards.note: Carrots are vegetables and hummus is made from chickpeas, a protein food. Apple and cheese or crackers and beans work the same way.

cards.q: Half the plate is fruits and vegetables. Grains fill one quarter. Which group fills the last quarter?
cards.note: The plate picture: half fruits and vegetables, a quarter grains, a quarter protein, and a cup of dairy on the side.

cards.q: On a balanced plate, what goes in the cup on the side?
cards.note: Dairy sits beside the plate. Milk, yogurt or fortified soy milk all work.

cards.q: Your plate has rice and chicken. What could you add to fill half the plate?
cards.note: Rice is grains and chicken is protein. Add broccoli or a salad and some fruit, and the plate is balanced.

cards.q: Your lunch is a cheese sandwich and milk. What is missing?
cards.note: Bread is grains, cheese and milk are dairy. Add an apple or carrot sticks.

cards.q: Yogurt, berries and granola for breakfast. How many food groups is that?
cards.note: Yogurt is dairy, berries are fruit, granola is grains. Three groups before school!

cards.q: Why is it nice to eat dinner together as a family?
cards.note: Family meals are for talking about your day. Kids who eat with family often try more foods.

cards.q: Everyone shares one big bowl of rice. Which spoon do you use to take some?
cards.note: A serving spoon keeps everyone's germs out of the shared bowl. Your own spoon goes in your own mouth only.

cards.q: Why do we sit down while we eat?
cards.note: Running or lying down with food in your mouth can make you choke. Sit, chew, swallow, then play.

cards.q: Your tummy takes a while to tell your brain it is full. So how should you eat?
cards.note: It takes about twenty minutes for the full signal to reach your brain. Eating slowly gives it time to arrive.

cards.q: Someone cooked dinner for you. What is a kind thing to say?
cards.note: Cooking takes work. A thank you makes the cook smile, even on nights you are not sure about the food.

cards.q: You want to help make dinner. Which job is a good one for a kid?
cards.note: Kids can wash veggies, tear lettuce, stir cold things and set the table. Hot and sharp jobs are for grown-ups.

cards.q: Before dinner, what can you set out for everyone at the table?
cards.note: Setting the table is a real help. One plate, one cup, and a fork or chopsticks for each person.

cards.q: A meal with food from many groups is called a...?
cards.note: Balanced means a bit of everything: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein and dairy.

cards.q: You eat a snack right before dinner. How does your tummy feel when dinner comes?
cards.note: Snack time works best a few hours before a meal, so your tummy is ready for dinner.
